svg.title: Developer journey — when something is wrong, init tells you exactly what to fix — init guides the developer through every misconfigured start
svg.text: Developer journey — when something is wrong, init tells
Scenario: init guides the developer through every misconfigured start

g.text: Given a developer's new project points at a GitLab remote the CLI never
signed into
A throwaway project whose only link to GitLab is a remote the CLI never signed into. Set up
off-camera: a fresh Ubuntu box with the toolbox and this git remote.
Then running init stops and shows the exact GitLab sign-in command to
run
init installs its tools, reaches the sign-in check and stops with "GitLab authentication
required", pointing at task glab:auth. The test also checks the command failed and printed
that line.
Then turning the GitLab integration off lets init finish cleanly
TASK_GLAB_ENABLED=false makes every glab step skip, so init reaches "DevSecOps project
initialization completed" and never asks about sign-in. The test also checks the command
succeeded and never printed "glab auth login".
When another developer's project points at a GitHub remote instead
A new project whose remote points at github.com — a non-GitLab host init must never push to.
The card shows the remote.
Then init refuses the non-GitLab remote and shows how to fix it
init finds no GitLab remote and stops with "No GitLab repository remote was detected.",
giving the exact git remote set-url line to fix it. The test also checks the command failed
and printed those lines.

svg.text: Storyboard e2e · 5 steps · 5 frames · every frame is its own pixel baseline (tolerance: 0)
